chosen.why_this_choice: Rule 3: no per-dataset results table exists for any metric, so the highest-priority metric (G-mean) is taken from the ranking table. Rule 4: abstract highlights no classifier; C4.5 is the first reported (Tables 2-3). higher_is_better=false because values are mean ranks (rank 1 = best).

Bonferroni-Dunn mean-rank difference MDO vs SMOTE (MAUC, C4.5, Table 3; CD = 1.2490)

stat_test: Iman-Davenport improved Friedman test (F_F) over 5 over-sampling methods x 20 data sets, with Bonferroni-Dunn post-hoc test using MDO as control (q_0.05 = 2.4980, CD = 1.2490); done per metric (MAUC, G-mean, precision, recall, F-measure) and per classifier (C4.5, KNN, Ripper). Friedman null rejected in all cases.

win_claim.quote: Our theoretical analyses and empirical observations across wide spectrum multi-class imbalanced benchmarks indicate that MDO is the method of choice by offering statistical superior MAUC and precision compared to the popular over-sampling techniques.

notes: Paper reports NO per-dataset metric values: only mean ranks (Tables 2, 4, 6) and Friedman/post-hoc rank differences (Tables 3, 5, 7), so rows is empty. Table 1 (PDF p.9, journal p.246) lists 20 UCI/KEEL data sets (e.g. Breast-tissue, Hayes-roth, Wine, Autos, ..., winequality-white, Letter). Precision/recall/F-measure are computed for the minority class only; G-mean is multi-class extended G-mean, MAUC is Hand-Till M-measure. Protocol: stratified 5-fold CV x 10 runs, Weka classifiers. Other classifiers' G-mean mean ranks (MDO / SMOTE): KNN Table 4 2.1000 / 2.4750; Ripper Table 6 2.1000 / 2.7750. Boldface significance marks in Tables 3/5/7 not verifiable from text extraction (pages not rendered). Single method, no variants.
